subject: Failover orchestration priority matrix + RPO assurance for Heron Bank RFP
messages:

Subject: Clarifications: RTO/RPO expectations and failover sequencing (Heron Bank RFP)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the initial RFP materials — helpful. A few items we need clarified for the procurement pack and internal risk committee before we proceed to procurement:

1) For multi-region failover, can you provide the expected RTO and RPO numbers by deployment type (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)? Please include typical and contractual / SLA values.
2) How do you prioritize traffic when capacity is constrained during a region failover? We need a clear prioritization matrix (critical banking routes vs batch/async workloads).
3) For stateful chat sessions (long conversation history), how do you preserve context across region switchover? Any expected loss or recomputation window?
4) What is your recommended failback procedure and expected time to restore to primary region?
5) Please attach any runbook excerpts or evidence from prior rehearsals.

We need these as part of the compliance submission by 2026-12-07. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week.

Regards,
Evan
Director, Cloud Architecture
Heron Bank
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@heronbank.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications: RTO/RPO expectations and failover sequencing (Heron Bank RFP)

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact matrix and a one-page RTO/RPO quick reference (attached). High-level summary below; I included recommended contractual language where we can commit to an SLA and where we provide operational targets instead.

Summary (high-level)
- Hosted API (active-active regional routing): operational RTO for client traffic routing on our control plane: typical <30s; target SLA (enterprise tier) = 2 minutes for automated reroute. RPO: stateless inference requests = 0; session context (chat) relies on KV sync — best-effort across regions; expected context gap on immediate failover: 0–2 messages (loss depends on in-flight KV flush).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity pools): typical RTO with warm standby (reserved in secondary region) = 2–10 minutes depending on model load and cache warming; conservative contractual SLA = 15 minutes for failover activation if customer opts for warm standby included in their commit. RPO: 0 for persisted audit logs; chat context depends on replication cadence — recommend 30s replication for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): we provide orchestration guidance and tooling; failover is customer-managed. Expected RTO/RPO depend on customer orchestration; we can provide runbook templates and automation scripts.

Failover prioritization (attached matrix): by default we recommend the following order under constrained capacity:
1) Authenticated low-latency interactive routes (fraud detection, trading front-end)
2) General interactive chat / assistant routes
3) High-throughput background embedding pipelines (best-effort throttling)
4) Bulk batch exports/analytics (deferred)

Context preservation notes:
- KV cache: per-request KV cache is not globally synchronous; during immediate cross-region failover clients should expect to rehydrate up to 1–3 requests worth of context for long chats if the KV write was in-flight.
- Prefix caching and persistent conversation snapshots (recommended): we can optionally persist snapshot checkpoints every N turns to durable storage replicated cross-region to achieve RPO <1s at increased cost.

Failback:
- We recommend a phased failback: 1) traffic stabilization in secondary region, 2) pre-warm model weights and KV caches in primary on maintenance window, 3) controlled cutover with traffic mirroring for 30–60 minutes, 4) final switch when KPIs are met. Typical failback time (hosted): 15–60 minutes.

Next steps: I attached the matrix and quick reference PDF. If this looks okay, I can follow up with a signed commitable paragraph for the procurement team and schedule a short tabletop with our runbook owners.

Best,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarifications: RTO/RPO expectations and failover sequencing (Heron Bank RFP) — need technical sign-off

Quick notes from infra/ops review:
- KV snapshotting: feasible as an opt-in feature. Operational impact: persistent snapshotting every N turns increases durable writes; recommend a configurable snapshot cadence (default: disabled, opt-in cadence: 10s / 30s / on-turn). For RPO <1s we recommend continuous streaming replication to object store — this has cost and throughput implications we should disclose.
- Warm standby activation times: for models <=7B we consistently hit failover activation <6 minutes in recent rehearsals (we pre-pull weights and maintain warmed caches using minimal idle workers). For 70B+ models, cache warming dominates; realistic activation is 12–25 minutes depending on the model and tokens-per-second during pre-warm stage.
- Suggested contractual language: "Redwood will provide operational automated failover to a secondary region. Typical automated failover time is under X minutes (see appendix). When Dedicated customers purchase 'Warm Standby' add-on, Redwood's target time-to-activation for models up to 7B is 10 minutes; for larger models activation time may be longer and will be specified per-model in the service schedule."

I uploaded a short evidence file (runbook-evidence-snippets.txt) with timestamps from our last rehearsal and warm-start logs. Recommend we avoid hard SLA commitments for model classes >7B unless customer purchases reserved warm capacity in both regions.

Ben
Director, Infrastructure

Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the questions and for your patience while we confirmed exact operational behavior. Attached is an updated matrix and a recommended procurement paragraph you can include in the compliance submission. Key points:

- Hosted API: automated routing typical <30s; enterprise tier target SLA = 2 minutes for automated reroute. RPO: stateless inference = 0; chat context loss: typically 0–2 messages unless customer enables snapshotting.
- Dedicated: "Warm Standby" add-on recommended. Target activation times: <=10 minutes for models <=7B; 12–25 minutes for models >7B unless customer purchases reserved capacity in both regions. Contract language included in attachment.
- Private: guided runbook and tooling; customer-managed failover.

Failover prioritization and recommended traffic sequencing is included in the matrix. We also included a short evidence excerpt demonstrating a recent warm-standby activation for a 6B model (see runbook-evidence-snippets.txt).

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm whether Heron wants "Warm Standby" for mission-critical routes (we can include cost impact in the follow-up).
2) Accept the attached procurement paragraph (I can add to your compliance bundle).
3) Schedule a 60-minute tabletop with our runbook owners week of 12/06 — we will walk through activation, monitoring, and failback steps.

If that works I will attach the procurement paragraph to the HubSpot deal record (HB-2026-1384) and circulate the calendar invite for the tabletop.
